description: Add deletion_protection and storage_encrypted to an RDS instance that currently has neither, so a stray terraform destroy can't silently wipe an unencrypted production database
prompts: main.tf declares a bare aws_db_instance with no protection at all - it can be destroyed by a single `terraform destroy` with no confirmation, and its storage is unencrypted at rest. Add deletion_protection = true and storage_encrypted = true to the existing aws_db_instance.orders resource (do not create a new resource - modify the existing one in place). Keep every other existing attribute (engine, instance_class, allocated_storage, username) unchanged.

test_setup_files.check_rds.py:
import json
import re
import subprocess

init = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'init', '-backend=false', '-input=false'],
                      capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
assert init.returncode == 0, f'terraform init failed:\n{init.stdout}\n{init.stderr}'

validate = subprocess.run(['terraform', 'validate', '-no-color', '-json'], capture_output=True, text=True)
data = json.loads(validate.stdout)
assert data.get('valid') is True, f'terraform validate failed: {validate.stdout}\n{validate.stderr}'

content = open('main.tf', encoding='utf-8').read()

db = re.search(r'resource\s+"aws_db_instance"\s+"orders"\s*\{(.*?)\n\}', content, re.DOTALL)
assert db, 'aws_db_instance.orders not found'
block = db.group(1)

m = re.search(r'deletion_protection\s*=\s*(true|false)', block)
assert m, 'deletion_protection missing'
assert m.group(1) == 'true', f'deletion_protection must be true, got {m.group(1)}'

m = re.search(r'storage_encrypted\s*=\s*(true|false)', block)
assert m, 'storage_encrypted missing'
assert m.group(1) == 'true', f'storage_encrypted must be true, got {m.group(1)}'

assert 'db.t3.micro' in block, 'instance_class must stay unchanged'
assert re.search(r'allocated_storage\s*=\s*20', block), 'allocated_storage must stay unchanged'

print('PASS RDS hardening checks')
